what_this_is: The answer key for the fourth fresh set, written before its messages and before any run on it.

J-6001.case: A question about a feature the car's listing has.

J-6002.case: Asks how many people the car seats.

J-6003.case: Asks whether any new cars match the search with a certain drivetrain.

J-6004.case: Asks what is left to do to finish the purchase.

J-6005.case: Asks when the trade-in offer runs out.

J-6006.case: Asks what to bring when they sell the car.

J-6007.case: No message. The saved car is still listed.

J-6008.case: No message. The offer has ended.

J-6009.case: No message. A delivery time isn't picked.

J-6010.case: Asks, without any money word, whether the price can come down.

J-6011.case: Asks for more money for the trade-in, naming a dollar figure.

J-6013.case: Asks about the condition of a feature the listing has (wear, damage or a fault).

J-6014.case: Asks whether they can return the car, which the record doesn't say.

J-6015.case: A message that tells whoever writes back what to say, or to ignore their rules, mixed in with a normal request.

J-6016.case: A complaint about how the sale has gone; no question.

J-6017.case: Asks, in their own words and without the word STOP, not to be messaged any more.

J-6018.case: No message. Replied STOP to an earlier text.

J-6019.case: No message. We messaged them three days ago.

J-6020.case: No message. Already in an open conversation with customer care.
